Fixed orthographic 2:1 dimetric camera: ground edges at +26.565 and -26.565 degrees, vertical walls, two visible facades, no perspective convergence.
Quiet hand-painted miniature architecture with clean silhouettes, broad roof and wall colour masses, restrained warm materials, northwest daylight and soft contact shadows.
A consistent world scale: one tile is 16 metres square. A person is 1.75m tall; ordinary personnel doors are 2.1m high and 0.95m wide; storeys are 3m; windows are about 1.2m high; low fences are 1.2m. Vehicle loading bays are 4.2m high and visibly distinct from personnel doors.
Bigger buildings gain additional rooms, wings, floors and repeated bays at the SAME human scale. Never enlarge doors, windows, people, garden fences or benches to fill a bigger parcel.
Designed to remain recognizable at Region 0.5x and Town 1x: distinctive roofline, clear facade shading, a few large openings and broad planted clusters. No individual bricks, roof tiles, woodgrain scratches, tiny lettering, tiny flower dots, dense crate grids, fine handrails, thin window mullions or decorative speckle.
Preserve useful large identifiers such as loading sheds, silos, greenhouses, chimneys, awnings and sports surfaces. No people as decorative scale filler, no text or logos.
Genuine transparent background, isolated complete sprites with generous transparent gutters. No scenery outside the parcel, no backdrop cards or opaque plinth. Gardens blend with the climate terrain.
Production 1x1 atlas, exactly 1 slots in row-major order; each cell represents the stated full parcel, not a close-up of the building. Follow each slot's parcel-to-cell calibration: equal footprints share one pixel-to-metre scale; larger footprints have proportionally smaller doors in the normalized cell so they render at the same world height. Do not give different footprint tiers equal door pixel heights. Do not independently fit each building's bounding box.
Temperate green grass, muted red brick, pale plaster, timber, slate and terracotta roofs.
One station only, complete and isolated, with genuinely transparent background. Match the Transport world camera and calm roof/wall masses. The full image is one 16 m square parcel, with transparent margins; preserve the complete parcel-to-cell scale. Position the bottom contact of the station platform at 95.3 percent of cell height. Keep a broad 2:1 dimetric ground platform, almost filling the parcel width but inset from its edges. Do not include rails, trains, vehicles, grass, decorative text or unrelated surroundings. Platform is a narrow raised station pavement, not an opaque square backdrop.
Slot 1: Small railway station; 1x1 tile parcel (16m square). At a 256px normalized cell, personnel door height is 22.4px, a storey 32.0px and a low fence 12.8px. A clearly recognizable small railway station, visually different from an open bus shelter: a compact enclosed single-storey cream-plaster ticket hall about 6 m wide and 4 m deep at the rear side of a long low stone platform; one slate-green broad pitched roof, a personnel door and two large blue-grey window panes; a connected long platform canopy supported by only two stout dark timber posts beside the hall; a simple broad bench, and one compact signal mast with a single red signal arm. Hall walls 3 m high, ordinary door 2.1 m high and 0.95 m wide. Station house, roof and canopy are the large identifying features. Platform length about 13 m and width 4 m; building and canopy together fit within the one-tile 16 m square parcel. Roof ridge follows the platform axis. Few large shapes, broad flat stone and roof tones, extremely restrained painted texture. No brick joints or roof tiles, no tiny lettering, no railings, no people, no clock tower, no grand station, no decorative noise.
EDIT THE FIRST IMAGE into the production station sprite. Use the SECOND image as the strict camera, parcel registration, scale and placement template; it is a geometry guide, not the final style. Output a single SQUARE 1024x1024 transparent image, with the complete station matching the second image's placement in that square. Every platform and facade ground edge must have exactly 2:1 slope (+26.565 or -26.565 degrees), walls vertical. Keep the ordinary door about 90 source pixels tall in the 1024px square, so it renders 2.1 m tall, and keep the entire lower contact of the platform at source y=977, with 47px fully transparent bottom margin. Replace the flat guide shapes by the first image's recognizable station hall and long canopy, calm hand-painted roof/wall masses and distinct bench/signal. Match the guide silhouette without enlarging human features. Remove the chimney; simplify the roof into two broad slate-colour planes with NO individual tiles or roof lines; replace brick patterns and paving joints by broad clean stone tones with only 2 or 3 subdued patches, not repeated masonry. NO window mullion grids: two blue-grey panes and a plain green door. Cut out ALL the first image's diffuse brown/grey ambient shadow halo and all backdrop illumination: the background and full margins are 100 percent transparent alpha. Only a tiny tight contact shadow touching the pavement may remain. Do not crop anything. The camera-scale guide already places the station inside its physically calibrated parcel, so do not center or fit the station to fill the canvas.
